name: perf-open-nonprofiler
why: perf_event_open() from a process outside the profiler allowlist is the anchor
source: synthetic: shape of normalize() output for perf_event_open_behavioral.c's record (attr ptr, pid 0, cpu -1, group -1). cpu/group are int -1 passed through glibc's variadic syscall(), so auditd logs a2/a3 as 'ffffffff' (32-bit), not sign-extended

name: perf-open-shell-tool
why: a shell-spawned binary opening a hardware counter is the same unexpected-process anchor; comm must not matter beyond the allowlist
source: synthetic: an ad-hoc tool calling perf_event_open on a hardware event (cpu 0, no group: group fd -1 is a3='ffffffff')

name: bpf-not-perf
why: bpf() is the other kernel-observability primitive a non-profiler might reach for; it keeps the surface but is not perf_event_open, so the syscall anchor must be load-bearing
source: synthetic: a bpf(BPF_PROG_LOAD=5) call from a non-profiler; a2 is sizeof(union bpf_attr)=0x90

name: ioctl-not-perf
why: PERF_EVENT_IOC_ENABLE is an ioctl() on an existing perf fd, not the perf_event_open syscall; same perf surface, different syscall, so it must not fire
source: synthetic: ioctl(PERF_EVENT_IOC_ENABLE) on a perf fd

name: perf-allowlisted
why: the perf tool opens counters by design; the comm allowlist alone must suppress it
source: recorded via benign slice: `perf record` sampling, comm 'perf' exe /usr/lib/linux-tools/.../perf

name: bpftrace-allowlisted
why: bpftrace opens perf events for its hardware/software/tracepoint probes via perf_event_open; comm is 'bpftrace' (basename of /usr/bin/bpftrace), which the comm allowlist suppresses
source: recorded via source: bpftrace calls perf_event_open for AttachProbe; comm 'bpftrace'

name: unrelated-read
why: an ordinary ioctl(fd, TCGETS) by a routine process: an audited syscall (atomic.rules records ioctl) that shares neither the anchored syscall nor its arguments -- a sanity floor that must stay quiet
source: synthetic: a routine ioctl(TCGETS), an audited high-volume syscall used as a non-firing floor

name: datadog-system-probe-filtered
why: the Datadog system-probe opens perf events for its eBPF probes; its comm is system-probe and its exe is under /opt/datadog-agent, never `datadog-agent`, so the old comm entry matched nothing. The profiler_images entry suppresses it (the old rule fired on it). system-probe runs as root from datadog-agent-sysprobe.service (no User=; the main Agent unit has User=dd-agent), with no login uid, which the entry's euid condition requires
source: Datadog Agent install root /opt/datadog-agent (docs.datadoghq.com agent configuration files); the exact binary path inside that tree is not recorded in this repository, so the filter matches the whole install tree; DataDog/datadog-agent pkg/fleet/installer/packages/embedded/tmpl/datadog-agent-sysprobe.service.tmpl (no User=) and datadog-agent.service.tmpl (User=dd-agent)

name: datadog-agent-comm-from-tmp
why: a binary that names itself datadog-agent still fires: the removed comm entry no longer lets that name evade the rule, and the Datadog entry now needs the Datadog install tree

name: system-probe-run-by-user-fires
why: an unprivileged user runs the Datadog system-probe binary under ptrace (or with LD_PRELOAD) and the injected perf_event_open keeps comm system-probe and its exe under /opt/datadog-agent, but carries the user's euid; profiler_images requires the root that the packaged system-probe runs as, so it fires. The rule without the euid condition suppressed this
source: synthetic from recorded mechanism: code injected into a non-setuid binary keeps its comm and exe (recorded for /usr/bin/gdb and /usr/bin/runc as uid 65534, see T1620 ldpreload-into-runc-as-exe-known-miss); uid/euid/auid of a user's login session

name: datadog-system-probe-root-euid-filtered
why: the packaged system-probe (root, no login uid) opening a perf event for an eBPF probe: euid 0 is what profiler_images needs beyond comm and exe, and the same event with an unprivileged euid fires (see system-probe-run-by-user-fires)
source: DataDog/datadog-agent datadog-agent-sysprobe.service.tmpl: ExecStart={{.InstallDir}}/embedded/bin/system-probe run, no User=; kernel/audit.c audit_log_task_info() (euid as %u)
